gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the only all-wheel-drive robot mower whose maker says it can 'operate rain or shine' is the Husqvarna Automower 435 iQ AWD at $4,999.99 (Husqvarna US, 2026-11-17), which is $2,500 more than the Segway Navimow X430 ($2,499) and $3,000 more than the Mammotion LUBA 3 AWD 3000 ($1,999), both of which head back to the dock when their rain sensing trips. It also has the lowest water rating in the group, IPX4 against IPX5 to IP66.
standout_why: MowScout (cited) lists only the 2WD-class Husqvarna 410 iQ and 420 iQ as rain-or-shine, says the 430X manual says to wait for wet grass to dry, gives no prices and never mentions the 435 iQ AWD. MowReview (cited) lists the 435 iQ AWD's area and slope but says nothing about wet grass and quotes no prices. Robovations prices only the LUBA 3 AWD 5000, Navimow i2 AWD and Dreame A3 AWD Pro 5000, with no Husqvarna. The Verge (cited) quotes launch prices but none for the 435 iQ AWD and nothing about which models are cleared for rain. ChatGPT itself wrote 'confirm the exact 435 iQ AWD guidance before purchasing'. Husqvarna's US product page settles that: it says rain or shine and lists IPX4.
decides: For a shopper who wants to keep mowing when the grass stays wet, especially on slopes, the 435 iQ AWD is the only pick that combines AWD with a maker rain-or-shine claim, and it costs a $2,500 to $3,000 premium. The LUBA 3 AWD and Navimow X430 are better value only if dry-day mowing is acceptable: the LUBA tears soft wet turf on turns (The Verge, with Mammotion's own admission), and the X430 skips mowing when its forecast predicts rain. On flatter lawns up to about an acre, the 420 iQ ($2,599.99, rain or shine, 45% slope) is the cheaper rain-cleared choice, but Husqvarna US shows it out of stock today. This confirms ChatGPT's first-chat Husqvarna lean and puts a price on it.
